# AKW-100 · Standard

The always-read part of the standard. Every rule below applies to any
Keynote. Read this file before drafting; do not work from memory.

A checklist row marked `carried below` needs no other file. A row naming a
file does: read that file when the row applies to the Keynote in hand.

## The rules

### rules/20-structure.md

**AKW-20.1** Every Parent Keynote is one of two types:

- **Complete**: the Parent is a full requirement and stands alone.
- **Stem**: the Parent is an opening that its Variants finish.

**AKW-20.2** A Complete Parent reads as a whole requirement with no Variant
present. Its Variants add a case; they do not change what the Parent already
requires.

**AKW-20.3** A Stem ends with a colon. Each Variant must form a grammatical
sentence when joined to the Stem. A Stem whose Variants are tagged
dispositions ends `AS TAGGED...` instead (AKW-20.11).

```
2    A LICENSED ELECTRICIAN, UNDER A SEPARATE PERMIT, IS RESPONSIBLE FOR:
2A     REDISTRIBUTION OF EXISTING LIGHTING (SEE RCP)
```

**AKW-20.4** A Stem prints in the Keynote Legend directly above its Variants,
indented one level. A Variant is never printed away from its Stem.

**AKW-20.5** A Variant never contradicts its Parent. **If it does, the Parent is
carrying too much.** Move the contested requirement down into the Variants and
the Parent becomes a Stem.

Before. `D3A` cancels `D3`:

```
D3    REMOVE FIXTURE. CAP AND REMOVE BACK TO THE SOURCE PANEL.
D3A   RETAIN AND RELOCATE EMERGENCY LIGHTING PER RCP.
```

After. The contested requirement moved down. The base keeps only what every
Variant performs:

```
D3    REMOVE EXISTING LIGHTING FIXTURE OR RECEPTACLE FROM ITS EXISTING
      LOCATION. PATCH AND REPAIR ANY DAMAGE AND PROVIDE CODE-COMPLIANT
      FIRE-STOPPING AS NEEDED. AS TAGGED...
D3A     ...CAP AND REMOVE THE ASSOCIATED CIRCUITING BACK TO THE SOURCE
        PANEL, OR TO THE NEAREST JUNCTION BOX
D3B     ...RETAIN AND RELOCATE EMERGENCY LIGHTING WITH ITS CIRCUITING
        PER PROPOSED RCP, ALIGN HEIGHTS WITH EXISTING ADJACENT LIGHTING
```

**AKW-20.6** `IN LIEU OF <parent number>,` is the only permitted override, and
only where the Keynote Legend has already been issued and renumbering would
break a bulletin or a filed set. It is not a substitute for AKW-20.5.

**AKW-20.7** A requirement is written once. Where it is needed again, reference
it, by Keynote Number, sheet, or schedule. Two copies of a requirement become
two different requirements at the first revision.

**AKW-20.8** A General Note carries no Keynote Tag and applies to the whole
sheet or set. It uses the prefix `G`. Because it has no tag, a General Note
**may** state its own Extent. This is the only exception to AKW-40.1. Every
other rule in AKW-100 applies to it unchanged.

**AKW-20.9** Every sentence in a Stem's text is performed at every location
where any of its Variants is tagged. Where a Variant would not perform a
sentence in the Stem - it retains what the Stem removes, or reuses what the
Stem discards - the base carries contested work. Move that sentence into the
affected Variants, or out into a separate Complete Keynote tagged at the same
location, before the set is issued.

**AKW-20.10** Every set carrying Variant Keynotes carries a General Note
stating the inclusion:

```
G1   WHERE A LOCATION IS TAGGED BY MORE THAN ONE KEYNOTE TAG, THE FULL
     REQUIREMENT OF EVERY TAG APPLIES AT THAT LOCATION. A LETTERED VARIANT
     KEYNOTE INCLUDES THE FULL TEXT OF ITS PARENT KEYNOTE.
```

The printed note is the only text a takeoff is certain to carry. The rules
above govern the writing; this one binds the bid.

**AKW-20.11** Where a Stem's Variants are tagged dispositions, the Stem ends
`AS TAGGED...` and every Variant is prefixed `...`. The ellipsis is the
continuation signal: the Variant is part of the Stem's text. A Stem whose
Variants complete its sentence ends with a colon and no ellipsis
(AKW-20.3). The ellipsis is a printed flag, not a contract; the General Note
per AKW-20.10 binds.

### rules/30-sentences.md

**AKW-30.1** A sentence has 25 words maximum.

**AKW-30.2** A Keynote has 5 sentences and 80 words maximum. A Parent and each
Variant are counted separately.

**AKW-30.3** Over either cap, split the Keynote into a Parent and Variants. The
caps exist to force that split. A note that will not fit is a note doing two
jobs.

**AKW-30.4** Write in the active voice, as an imperative.

- Write: `CLEAN, PATCH, AND REPAIR ALL PARTITIONS.`
- Not: `ALL PARTITIONS SHALL BE CLEANED, PATCHED, AND REPAIRED.`

**AKW-30.5** One idea per sentence. A comma splice is a defect. Two independent
clauses joined by a comma become two sentences.

- Defect: `VENDOR SHALL VERIFY ALL CONDITIONS, IF SCOPE REQUIRES RELOCATION...`
- Fixed: `VENDOR SHALL VERIFY ALL CONDITIONS. IF SCOPE REQUIRES RELOCATION...`

**AKW-30.6** The default Actor is the general contractor, declared once in a
General Note. A Keynote names an Actor **only** when the work is not the general
contractor's: a separate-permit trade, a vendor, an owner-supplied installer.

Naming the general contractor on some notes and not others invites the question
of who performs the unnamed ones.

**AKW-30.7** `SHALL` states a condition the finished work must hold. The
imperative states an action to perform. Prefer the imperative.

- Action: `REPAINT ALL SURFACES TO MATCH EXISTING IN KIND.`
- Condition: `A RISE OVER 3 IN. SHALL BE RAMPED, NOT STEEPER THAN 1:12.`

**AKW-30.8** Do not open a Keynote with a courtesy or a hedge. No `PLEASE NOTE`,
`IT IS INTENDED THAT`, `THE CONTRACTOR IS ADVISED`. Start with the verb or the
subject of the work.

### rules/40-words.md

**AKW-40.1** A Keynote states **what** work is required and **what end
condition** the work must be left in.

It does not state **means and methods**: the contractor's sequence, technique,
equipment, labour, or safety.

It does not state **Extent**: where the work is or how much of it there is. The
Keynote Tag carries Extent. Holding Extent out of the words is what makes one
Keynote serve every location.

Naming a **termination point** or a **physical end state** is scope, not method:

```
CAP AND REMOVE BACK TO THE SOURCE PANEL, OR TO THE NEAREST JUNCTION BOX
```

That fixes where the work stops. How the conductor is pulled stays the
electrician's business.

**AKW-40.2** Vagueness about Extent is permitted **only** when something else
decides it: a stated trigger, or a Reference Document.

| Phrase | Verdict | Decider |
|--------|---------|---------|
| `AS SCHEDULED` | Pass | The schedule |
| `PER PROPOSED RCP` | Pass | The RCP |
| `IN KIND` | Pass | The existing product |
| `TYPICAL, U.O.N.` | Pass | The notes that say otherwise |
| `AS NEEDED IF THE CONDITION UNCOVERS A VOID` | Pass | The stated trigger |
| `AS NEEDED` (bare) | **Fail** | Nothing |
| `AS REQUIRED` (bare) | **Fail** | Nothing |
| `WHERE INDICATED` (bare) | **Fail** | Nothing |

**AKW-40.3** Vagueness about the **end condition** is banned outright. No
decider can rescue it, because the end condition is what the Keynote exists to
fix.

Banned words and phrases:

```
MAKE GOOD        MINOR          ADEQUATE       PROPER
SUITABLE         REASONABLE     NEAT           WORKMANLIKE
AS APPROPRIATE   TO SUIT        GOOD CONDITION ACCEPTABLE
```

Replace the adjective with the condition:

- Defect: `MAKE MINOR REPAIRS TO THE HANDRAILS.`
- Fixed: `REPAIR TO A SOUND SURFACE, FREE OF FLAKING COATING, RUST, AND
  CORROSION, READY FOR COATING.`

The condition sets the limit of work. An adjective never does.

**AKW-40.4** `NOT LIMITED TO` widens scope in the contractor's favour, not
yours. It is banned unless widening is the deliberate intent, and then the
Keynote must also state the end condition that closes it.

**AKW-40.5** State a slope limit as `NOT STEEPER THAN 1:8` or `NOT FLATTER THAN
1:48`. `MIN.` and `MAX.` are banned next to a ratio.

A slope ratio inverts: a bigger second number means a gentler slope. `MINIMUM
SLOPE OF 1:8` reads to a contractor as permission to build 1:6, and they are
reading it correctly.

`MIN.` and `MAX.` remain legal with a plain dimension: `3 IN. MIN.`

**AKW-40.6** Use `DAMAGE`, never `DAMAGES`. In a contract document *damages*
means money awarded in a lawsuit.

**AKW-40.7** Write `AND`. The ampersand `&` is not a word and is easy to lose at
plot scale.

**AKW-40.8** A slash `/` means **or**. It is permitted only where either reading
is acceptable. Where both items are required, write `AND`.

- `ALTER/AFFECT`: either reading is acceptable. Pass.
- `POWER/LOW-VOLTAGE`: both are required. **Fail.** Write `POWER AND
  LOW-VOLTAGE`.

**AKW-40.9** Do not abbreviate a verb. `PREP` becomes `PREPARE`. Abbreviate
units only, per AKW-50.2.

**AKW-40.10** Name the thing precisely. `FLOORS` is not `FLOOR FINISHES`. `TRIM`
is not `CORNER GUARDS, WALL PROTECTION, AND BASE MOLDING`. A subcontractor
prices the cheapest defensible reading of the word you wrote.

**AKW-40.11** One term per concept, across the whole set. The canonical terms
are in `CONTEXT.md`. Do not vary a term for style.

### rules/50-typography.md

**AKW-50.1** Keynote text is ALL CAPS.

**AKW-50.2** Abbreviate units. Put one space between the number and the unit.

```
3 IN.        1/4 IN.        10 MM        8 FT.
```

**AKW-50.3** Never use the inch mark `"` or the foot mark `'`. They are lost in
CAD fonts, in scanned sets, and in PDF text search, and they collide with quote
marks.

**AKW-50.4** Default to imperial units. Where the prompt or the project is
metric, follow it. Do not convert a unit that belongs to a product's own name:
`10 MM RUBBER FLOORING` stays as the manufacturer sells it.

**AKW-50.5** Underline a product called out by name.

**AKW-50.6** Write a ratio as `1:12`. No spaces, no word "to".

**AKW-50.7** Do not use quote marks for emphasis. In a Keynote a quote mark
reads as an inch mark.

- Defect: `REMOVE EXISTING ELECTRICAL 'FIXTURE' OR 'OUTLET'`
- Fixed: `REMOVE EXISTING LIGHTING FIXTURE OR RECEPTACLE`

**AKW-50.8** Write a fraction as `1/4`, not a decimal and not a typographic
fraction glyph.

**AKW-50.9** A parenthesis must close. An unbalanced parenthesis in an issued
Keynote is a defect, not a typo, because the reader cannot tell where the aside
was meant to end.
